item.title: Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Kyiv, Ukraine (November 17, 2026)
item.content:encoded:
Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Kyiv, Ukraine (November 17, 2026)

Location: Ukraine, all districts

Event: Due to attacks on Ukraine’s critical civilian infrastructure, the U.S. Embassy in Kyiv urges U.S. citizens in Ukraine to exercise heightened caution. These attacks may result in power outages, loss of heating, loss of water, and disruption of municipal services. The Department of State continues to advise U.S. citizens not to travel to Ukraine.

Actions to Take: 

  • Keep reserves of water, food, supplies, required medications, and other essentials.

item.title: Security Alert: Holiday Travel, November 13, 2026
item.content:encoded:
Security Alert: Holiday Travel, November 13, 2026

Location: Europewide

Event:  As the holiday season approaches, U.S. citizens across Europe should remain vigilant of their surroundings and practice sound personal security and situational awareness.  Large gatherings and public events may present a target of opportunity for terrorist groups and criminals.  Terrorists – including lone actors – may attack with little or no warning, targeting tourist locations such as markets, transportation hubs, shopping malls, place of worship, and other public areas.

U.S. citizens should exercise extra vigilance at holiday festivals and events and other locations with large crowds.  Visitors to congested and popular tourist areas should pay particular attention to their surroundings and always follow the instructions of police and emergency response officials.

Disruptions to travel and daily life remain possible across Europe during the holiday season.  Strikes and demonstrations have occurred with greater frequency in recent months across Europe.  In November, hoax bomb threats targeted civil aviation in numerous European countries, disrupting flights.  Americans should monitor local news during holiday travel abroad to stay informed about local events or developments that could disrupt transportation or daily life.  We encourage all U.S. citizens abroad to enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive the latest security updates for their destinations.

Actions to Take:

  • Remain alert.

item.title: ALERT – MESSAGE FOR U.S. CITIZENS: CONSULAR OFFICERS FROM THE U.S. EMBASSY TO OFFER SERVICES TO ALL U.S. CITIZENS IN LVIV
item.content:encoded:
ALERT – MESSAGE FOR U.S. CITIZENS: CONSULAR OFFICERS FROM THE U.S. EMBASSY TO OFFER SERVICES TO ALL U.S. CITIZENS IN LVIV ON NOVEMBER 5
Services are by appointment only and available for all U.S. citizens

Event:  U.S. Embassy Kyiv will offer American Citizens Services in Lviv.  Services are by appointment only and available for all U.S. citizens.

Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026

Time:  9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 1:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Location:  America House, 2 Akademika Hnatyuka St., Lviv

How to schedule an appointment:  Please email the following information to [e-mail removed]:

  • Full Name
  • Passport Number
  • Date of Birth
  • Type of Service
  • In the subject line mention ACS Services Lviv

Deadline: Friday, October 30, 2026, at 4:00 p.m.

After we confirm your appointment, we will email you instructions. Please read them carefully to avoid delays.

Available Services:

  • U.S. Passport Applications
  • Notarial Services
